name: code

edits.disables: All VS Code telemetry tiers (crash, error, usage). Supersedes deprecated telemetry.enableTelemetry / telemetry.enableCrashReporter — never write both.

persistent_files.note: Default-profile global state and extension storage under the supported user-data root. Named profiles and custom user-data roots require active-location inspection.
Timestamped IDE logs under the supported user-data root. A custom logsPath or user-data root requires active-location inspection.

cli_flags.note: Diagnostic / per-invocation flag (e.g. `code tunnel --disable-telemetry`); not a persistent opt-out.

commands.win32: powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command 'try { if (Get-Process -ErrorAction Stop | Where-Object { $_.ProcessName -eq "Code" }) { exit 0 }; exit 1 } catch { [Console]::Error.WriteLine($_); exit 2 }'

process_check.if_running: Quit VS Code before editing settings.json — graceful-shutdown rewrite can clobber manual edits.

notes: telemetry.telemetryLevel is the one canonical key — never double-write the deprecated enableTelemetry / enableCrashReporter alongside it.

Settings and persistent-file maps cover the supported platform roots; Linux uses XDG_CONFIG_HOME, defaulting to ~/.config when empty or unset. VSCODE_APPDATA, portable mode and --user-data-dir can redirect the active root, and logsPath can redirect logs. Resolve those locations before applying settings or claiming retained-state coverage. Existing named profiles can override settings and store their own global state; inspect them before claiming all-profile coverage.

Microsoft's NativeEnvironmentService resolves the platform root with getUserDataPath. AbstractNativeEnvironmentService joins that root with User/globalStorage for default-profile state and logs/<timestamp> for logs: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/environment/common/environmentService.ts. Platform roots and supported overrides: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/environment/node/userDataPath.ts.

caveats.framing: If github.copilot / github.copilot-chat extensions are installed (check ~/.vscode/extensions/), they DO NOT inherit telemetry.telemetryLevel per Microsoft docs. Check each extension's own telemetry docs separately. Skill never auto-writes Copilot-specific keys.
